subject: general
question: The International Space Station was launched in ______.
solution:
The correct answer is __**1998**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **International Space Station (ISS)** is a large-scale modular space station located in **low Earth orbit (LEO)**. It serves as a habitable artificial satellite and a major international research facility.
 
• The launch of the first component of the ISS took place on **November 20, 1998**. This initial module was named **Zarya** (meaning "Sunrise" in Russian), which provided electrical power, storage, propulsion, and guidance to the station during the initial stage of assembly. ***Hence, the year 1998 is correct.***
 
• The project is a joint endeavor involving five participating space agencies: **NASA** (United States), **Roscosmos** (Russia), **JAXA** (Japan), **ESA** (Europe), and **CSA** (Canada). The ownership and use of the station are established by intergovernmental treaties and agreements.
 
• Following the **Zarya** module, the second module, **Unity** (Node 1), was launched by the **United States** on **December 4, 1998**, aboard the Space Shuttle **Endeavour**, marking the first time components from different nations were joined in space.
 
• Continuous human presence on the **ISS** began on **November 2, 2000**, with the arrival of **Expedition 1**. Since then, the station has never been without a crew.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Physical Characteristics and Orbit:**

 
 
• The **ISS** orbits at an average **altitude of 400 kilometers (250 miles)** above the Earth's surface.
 
• It travels at a staggering speed of approximately **28,000 kilometers per hour (17,500 mph)**, which allows it to complete an entire orbit around the Earth every **90 minutes**.
 
• The total mass of the station is nearly **450,000 kilograms (approximately 1 million pounds)**, and it covers an area equivalent to a **football field**.
 
 
 
• **Scientific Purpose:**
 
 
• The station functions as a **microgravity and space environment research laboratory**. It allows scientists to conduct experiments in biology, human biology, physics, astronomy, and meteorology that would be impossible to perform on Earth.
 
• Key research includes studying the **long-term effects of space exposure** on the human body, which is critical for future missions to **Mars** and the **Moon**.
 
 
 
• **Discussion of Other Options:**
 
 
• **1965**: This **year** is famous for the first spacewalk by **Aleksei Leonov** and the **Gemini missions**, but it predates the **ISS** by decades. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• **1972**: This **year** marked the final **Apollo lunar mission** (**Apollo 17**) and the transition toward the **Skylab** program. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• **2004**: By this **year**, the **ISS** was already fully operational and inhabited by its ninth and tenth permanent crews. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **End of Mission:** The **ISS** is currently scheduled to operate until **2030**. **NASA** has developed a transition plan to deorbit the station safely into a remote part of the **Pacific Ocean**, known as **Point Nemo**, in early **2031**.
 
• **International Cooperation:** The **ISS** is widely regarded as one of the most complex engineering and political feats in human history, demonstrating that multiple **countries** can collaborate on long-term peaceful scientific endeavors.
 
• **The Zvezda Module:** Launched in **July 2000**, the **Zvezda Service Module** provided the early living quarters and life support systems, enabling the first permanent crew to reside on the station.
